chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid Al-Sayrafi, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about this matter, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' I said to him: 'There was a slave girl for me, but she was not granted a child from me. So I sold her, and she gave birth to a child from someone else, and I have a child from another woman. So, can I marry my child from another woman to her child?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You can marry [your child] to what was for her from the child before you,' meaning before she came to be for you.
ai.seo_question: Can a master marry his own child to the child of his former slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Reza (AS) clarifies the specific legal status of offspring from a slave girl (Umm Walad) who was sold by her master, establishing that her child belongs to the new owner. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the child's lineage and ownership are determined by the time of birth relative to the master's possession, thereby permitting marriage between the master's son and the slave's daughter. This ruling underscores the flexibility in marital alliances within the extended family structure in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about this problem, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Repeat it to me<sup>asws</sup>’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There used to be a slave girl for me, but she was not Graced with a child from me. So I sold her, and she gave birth to children from someone else, and for me are children from other than her. So, can I give my children from other than her in marriage to her children?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You can give in marriage to what was for her from the children before you, before she came to be for you’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about this case and he asked me to say it again and I said, ‘I had a slave-girl and I was not fortunate to have a child from her so I sold her and she give birth to a child from someone other than me and I have a child from a woman other than her; if I can give in marriage my child from another woman to her child.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You can give in marriage to her children who were before you, before she became yours.’”
